headline: High: Notion AI can leak workspace content into a broad-egress gateway, and shared workspace state creates prompt-injection and write-conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI ingests workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and can route agentic traffic. Because Notion shares workspace state across instances, attacker-controlled page content could influence downstream prompts if copied or re-used. The interaction is plausible, but not documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Notion page content is reused as prompt input to plano
IF plano forwards untrusted text into downstream model prompts without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate untrusted workspace content from prompt templates
Add provenance tags before passing Notion output to plano
Review any prompt concatenation logic for instruction-like text
Disable automatic reuse of page text in downstream prompts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and its vendor-hosted backend calls downstream model providers. Plano has broad network egress and processes logs, traces, and metrics. If Notion content is forwarded into plano or plano logs prompt payloads, sensitive workspace data can leave the workspace boundary. The shared path is plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Notion workspace content is sent through plano
IF plano logs or exports prompt payloads containing workspace text
mitigations: Restrict plano to redacted inputs only
Turn off verbose request logging for prompt payloads
Use a test workspace with non-sensitive pages
Review outbound destinations for Notion-derived text
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, while plano only shows a config.yaml file surface and no write or git capability. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is indirect shared workspace or config handling, so I keep this low rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same mutable config file
IF an external orchestrator grants plano write access not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep Notion and plano on separate workspaces
Store plano config in a read-only mount
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Check orchestrator permissions before pairing
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that could consume generated text. If plano treats Notion output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream routing or actions. Because no verification step is documented, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF plano uses Notion-generated text as a source of truth
IF downstream automation acts on that text without human review
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Notion output
Add a verification step against source pages
Label Notion output as untrusted in plano
Limit plano to summarization, not execution
requires-engineering: implement citation-based validation

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to downstream model providers, while plano has broad egress and processes logs and traces. If regulated workspace data is routed through plano, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific residency mismatch, so I avoid high and choose medium on the documented data-flow risk.
conditions: IF regulated data from Notion is forwarded into plano
IF plano retains logs longer than the workspace policy
mitigations: Use non-regulated data for the pair
Review retention settings on plano logs
Confirm vendor DPAs before production use
Minimize fields sent from Notion to plano
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
